source.title: Shared Emotion Geometry Across Small Language Models: A Cross-Architecture Study of Representation, Behavior, and Methodological Confounds

record.tranche_reason: Measures cross-model emotion-geometry similarity with cosine RDMs and RSA, a conceptual test of representational convergence using a different setting from the original claims. It also tests how extraction conditions affect the measured similarity.
record.gate_note: The paper measures emotion-vector RDM similarity across SLMs, so it bears on cross-model convergence. It does not test vision-language alignment, seed-wise convergence, feature or circuit recurrence, or representation mapping. The scale–maturity correlations concern geometry descriptors, not whether cross-model alignment increases with scale. Cited results from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures cross-architecture representational similarity (Spearman correlation of 21-emotion cosine RDMs) across independently trained small LMs from five mature families plus Gemma-3, at 1B–8B. That is a new setting with its own results on whether different models converge (V1), on how complete the alignment is and what drives it (V7, family lineage), and a small check of metric choice (V6, Spearman vs Pearson). The extraction-protocol and precision contrasts are within-model comparisons, not cross-model convergence measurements.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that five mature SLM families share a nearly identical 21-emotion geometry (ρ 0.74–0.92) despite opposed behavioural profiles, and that family lineage gives the strongest alignment. Gemma-3 1B is an immature, unreliable outlier that RLHF restructures. Sharpness descriptors scale with size, and extraction method, sub-parameters and precision strongly change extracted RDMs. They explicitly leave unresolved whether shared objective, shared data or language structure causes the convergence.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a fixed comprehension-mode emotion extraction pipeline and cosine-RDM Spearman comparisons across SLMs, rather than testing same-seed convergence, cross-modal alignment, or transferable representation mappings.
record.method_sensitivity: RDM similarity varies with comprehension versus generation extraction, generation sub-parameters, and fp16 versus INT8 precision. Gemma-3’s extreme anisotropy is flagged as making raw cosine-RDM comparisons unreliable; independent linear normalization of each RDM does not change the correlation.

fits_no_version.finding: Within a single model, the extracted emotion RDM changes drastically with extraction method, generation sub-parameters and precision. Comprehension vs generation gives ρ 0.091 to 0.355; sub-parameters give 0.02–0.03; fp16 vs INT8 gives 0.215 to 0.527.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept-vector geometry read from one model is highly sensitive to the extraction protocol, so cross-study convergence comparisons that mix protocols may be unreliable.

fits_no_version.finding: Base and instruct versions of the same mature family have near-identical emotion RDMs (ρ 0.918–0.985). Gemma-3 base vs instruct is ρ 0.190.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-training preserves concept geometry in mature base models but restructures it in immature ones.

fits_no_version.finding: Anisotropy and RDM std fall with model size (ρ −0.82 to −0.89). Best-layer depth tracks family more than size (ρ −0.48, p = 0.11).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single-model geometry descriptors mature with scale.

record.problems: The authors note small coverage: six architectural families, one immature-regime model, a single behavioral pair, and only two models in the precision analysis. Gemma-3 base has fp16 numerical instability beyond about layer 12. The study does not test whether shared training data or objectives explain convergence, and its size correlations are not tests of an alignment-versus-scale trend.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results on the claim were left out. Figure 1’s pairwise values are retained where text gives the result as an aggregate or names the comparison; other figure cells are not separately extracted.

untested.parts: Capability as a predictor of alignment. Scales beyond 8B. Non-decoder architectures and other objectives. Only one within-family scale pair.
Entire version: no vision-language or paired image-caption comparison.
Entire version: no different-seed runs of the same architecture.
Entire version: no mapping, stitching, relative representations or unpaired alignment. The authors note that vectors cannot be moved between models without a learned alignment.
Entire version: no neuron, SAE-feature or circuit recurrence.

Neighbour-based metrics and their settings. Other stimulus vocabularies or languages. Out-of-distribution inputs. Cross-model convergence under generation-mode extraction or other precisions. Isotropization of the vectors.
Plateau with scale. Causal isolation of shared data or objectives: the authors list three explanations and say they cannot adjudicate.

missing.what: Pair-group comparison of cross-model RDM alignment by size class. Sub-4B mature pairs: n=3, mean 0.825, range 0.813–0.842. 7B+ pairs: n=7, mean 0.838, range 0.742–0.919. Gemma-3 instruct pairs: n=5, mean 0.575. Authors: adding 7B+ models does not pull the distribution upward.

Per-model Gemma-3 1B base correlations (e.g. Mistral base 0.171, Qwen base 0.252, Gemma instruct 0.190), tightly clustered around 0.21. Authors argue raw cosine RSA is unreliable above anisotropy 0.95, but test no alternative metric.

record.verdict_notes: I classify this as T3 rather than T2: RSA on emotion concept vectors in SLMs is a new setting. The Figure 1 cell values are legible in the text extraction, so rows r01–r20 are not figure-only. The instruct pairs largely duplicate the base pairs, and r28, r29, r31 and r32 are duplicates or aggregates. The authors' anisotropy argument bears on V6 as an argument only: it is not demonstrated with an alternative metric, so it carries no label. RDMs here are cosine geometries of 21 concept vectors; a researcher should not read them as whole-representation alignment.

versions.untested_parts: The study compares models at different sizes but does not test whether cross-model alignment rises monotonically with size or capability, and does not measure capability as a predictor of alignment.
No comparison of independently seeded runs of the same architecture.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment test.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features, neurons, or circuits.

The study tests extraction-protocol and precision sensitivity and discusses anisotropy and linear RDM normalization. It does not test varying neighbour counts, alternative inputs, or out-of-distribution inputs; it does not validate nonlinear or vector-level isotropization.
The study reports incomplete alignment in some settings and family effects, but does not isolate shared training data or objectives as causes, and does not test whether alignment plateaus.

relationships.condition: Comprehension-mode 21-emotion cosine RDMs across five independently trained decoder families (1.5B–8B) vs the smallest model, Gemma-3 1B instruct
relationships.reason: All mature cross-family pairs align at ρ 0.74–0.92 despite different architectures and data (r01–r20, r28). The smallest, least mature model aligns less (ρ 0.53–0.63, r27).
relationships.display_finding: Mature cross-family pairs aligned at ρ = 0.74–0.92, while the smallest, least mature model aligned at ρ = 0.53–0.63.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Comprehension-mode 21-emotion cosine RDMs across five independently trained decoder families (1.5B–8B) vs the smallest model, Gemma-3 1B instruct
source_check.reason: High mature-model similarity versus one highly anisotropic smaller outlier does not establish increasing alignment as models grow or become more capable. Size, family and measurement reliability are confounded in this contrast.

relationships.reason: Alignment does not rise with size: per Figure 4 (text, no row), sub-4B pairs average 0.825 and 7B+ pairs 0.838. Qwen 1.5B × Llama 3.1 8B is lowest at 0.742 (r04). Lineage dominates: the Llama 3.2 × 3.1 pair is highest (r31, r32).
relationships.display_finding: Sub-4B pairs average 0.825 alignment versus 0.838 for 7B+ pairs; Qwen 1.5B × Llama 3.1 8B scores lowest at 0.742, while the Llama 3.2 × 3.1 pair scores highest.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Figure 4 explicitly reports that adding 7B+ models does not shift alignment upward: means 0.825 versus 0.838 with overlapping distributions. This is an absent scale-related increase in the tested mature regime, rather than merely an untested extension.

relationships.reason: The Llama 3.2 × Llama 3.1 pair (ρ 0.919 instruct, 0.910 base) exceeds every cross-family pair despite the scale gap. Authors attribute this to a shared lineage and data signature (r31, r32, r09, r19).
relationships.display_finding: Llama 3.2–Llama 3.1 correlations reached 0.919 for instruct models and 0.910 for base models, exceeding every cross-family pair; authors attributed this to shared lineage and data signatures.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: §3.4 reports the strongest instruct alignment for the Llama lineage pair, 0.919, with base alignment 0.910, and interprets this as a lineage signature. This supports a lineage association; it does not isolate shared-data causation.

relationships.reason: Alignment is incomplete (ρ 0.74–0.92, mean 0.834) but not far from complete. Authors call it nearly identical geometry and say its cause is unresolved (r01–r20, r28).
relationships.display_finding: Cross-family emotion geometry correlations ranged from ρ=0.74 to 0.92, averaging 0.834, while the cause of this agreement remained unresolved.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: The restricted emotion geometry is highly aligned, though incomplete: instruct range 0.742–0.919, mean 0.834. This qualifies the far-from-complete component of V7 without establishing complete convergence or explaining its cause.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Comprehension-mode 21-emotion cosine RDMs across five independently trained decoder families (1.5B–8B) vs the smallest model, Gemma-3 1B instruct
labels.reason: High mature-model similarity versus one highly anisotropic smaller outlier does not establish increasing alignment as models grow or become more capable. Size, family and measurement reliability are confounded in this contrast.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.reason: Figure 4 explicitly reports that adding 7B+ models does not shift alignment upward: means 0.825 versus 0.838 with overlapping distributions. This is an absent scale-related increase in the tested mature regime, rather than merely an untested extension.

labels.label: supports
labels.reason: §3.4 reports the strongest instruct alignment for the Llama lineage pair, 0.919, with base alignment 0.910, and interprets this as a lineage signature. This supports a lineage association; it does not isolate shared-data causation.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.reason: The restricted emotion geometry is highly aligned, though incomplete: instruct range 0.742–0.919, mean 0.834. This qualifies the far-from-complete component of V7 without establishing complete convergence or explaining its cause.

relation.reason: Its own cross-model comparisons, size-group analysis and methodological comparisons bear on the claim versions.

tranche.reason: The study supplies original convergence measurements in the new setting of comprehension-derived emotion geometry across small language models.

source_check.notes: Code release and methodological controls are explicitly reported; the capability flag concerns behavioral task screening, not capability-driven convergence. The text contains internal inconsistencies, including Gemma base's minimum correlation and §4.3's B/D condition definitions for the claimed clean sub-parameter contrast.

statements.correction: §2.8 reports release of extraction scripts, analysis scripts, a cross-backend unit test and intermediate outputs. §§2.4 and 4.3 report methodological controls. Mature instruct pairs: ρ = 0.742–0.919; Gemma instruct: 0.527–0.625, with anisotropy 0.982. No capability–alignment predictor analysis is reported.
statements.problem: The numerical contrast is correct, but no reported code or controls is false. Capability checks concern behavioral constraint tasks, not capability as an alignment predictor. The contrast does not establish V1.

statements.correction: Figure 4: sub-4B mature pairs mean 0.825; pairs involving a 7B+ model mean 0.838, with overlapping distributions and no upward distribution shift. §3.4: lineage preservation dominates the available within-family scale contrast.
statements.problem: The study-specific factual description is correct, but the stated absence of an upward size trend fits challenges for this tested condition under the verdict rules.

statements.correction: No independently measured capability–alignment analysis is reported. §2.7 capability checks screen behavioral constraint-following scenarios. §3.5 relates size and width to geometric descriptors.
statements.problem: The analysis is unreported, but the study does not explicitly identify independently measured capability as an untested alignment predictor.

statements.correction: §3.1: mature instruct emotion-RDM correlations 0.742–0.919, mean 0.834. §5.1: shared objectives, overlapping corpora and language structure remain unresolved explanations. For this study's condition, limits_scope is justified rather than challenges.
statements.problem: The range and mean are correct. These high but incomplete correlations qualify V7 for a restricted construct; they do not demonstrate the absence or reversal of partial convergence or settle its cause.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Mature SLM pairs across the tested 1.5B–8B range and the Llama cross-generation comparison
reader_labels.reason: RDM similarity is high across mature models, but the study does not show that alignment increases with size or capability; family lineage is prominent. Rows r01–r25 and r28–r32.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Extraction method, generation sub-parameters, precision, and high-anisotropy Gemma-3 comparisons
reader_labels.reason: RDM similarity changes substantially with extraction conditions, and the authors warn that raw cosine comparisons for highly anisotropic Gemma-3 are unreliable; linear per-RDM normalization does not change the correlation. Rows r26–r27 and r33–r41.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Mature models show strong but non-identical RDM alignment, while Gemma-3 comparisons are much weaker and flagged as unreliable; family lineage is also associated with closer alignment. These results qualify a simple universal-convergence account but do not establish its cause. Rows r01–r28 and r31–r32.
